sections.en: 1 Excerpts of Julian of Laodicea are not rare in manuscript books. In Vindobonensis ph. gr. 261, f. 79r-91v is found Ἰουλιανοῦ Λαοδικέως ἐπίσκεψις ἀστρονομική ('Astronomical examination of Julian of Laodicea') whose beginning is also preserved in our cod. 11, f. 247, c. 75. A chapter of the same περὶ καταρχῶν ('on inceptions') you will find below (p 138). Three fragments περὶ πολέμου ('on war') "from an old Vatican codex" Mai edited in Sript. vet. nov. coll., Rome 1827, II, 675 s. An excerpt περὶ ἀγορασμοῦ ('on buying') exists in Vindob. 115, f. 159r. Marc. 334, f. 52v. Cf. Kroll, Breslauer Abhand., VII, 1 (1894), p. 72. Philologus, N. F. XI. 1898, p. 125. The age of the very famous writer is uncertain.

summary.headline: Rain Omens and Saturn’s Nature
summary.text: Astrological rain omens based on planetary transits, trines, malefic testimony, pivots, Aries, Libra, and the preceding conjunction or full moon. The text then begins Julian’s account of the seven stars, describing Saturn’s cold, moist, slow nature and its effects on weather, animals, fruits, seas, winds, earthquakes, and chasms.
